_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Zero uses in ch. 15 — a siege/action chapter that reached for several manner-clause 'the way X did Y' constructions in early drafting and had every one of them rewritten to a plain 'as' clause or cut outright. Four of the last five chapters now at zero or one. The cap is holding better than the status implies; consider demoting to 'rest' if ch. 16 also comes in at zero.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Sixth chapter running at zero. Not reached for at all in ch. 15, including under pressure in the fight scenes where a vague placeholder would have been the easy way out.

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: Sixth chapter running at zero. One draft pass reached for a general 'I'd learned by then to...' rule during the quiet gathering beat and it was cut in favour of a concrete physical image (steady hands, folders coming off a shelf). Stays on watch.

Ch. 15 landed at 22, same low-to-mid-20s band as ch. 7-14. Contrast partner rotated again: Lloyd's long, accreting sentences (the plan, the catalogue of what Maria won't burn, the stair fight's single extended clauses) now pulled up short by Edie's and Maria's flat one-line calls in combat ('go.' / 'We're burning it' last chapter) rather than by institutional paperwork (ch. 14) or a second character's dialogue register generally. Keep rotating.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: One clean, isolated use again (Lloyd's job on the stair, 'same as it had been going down'). Four of the last five chapters at exactly one use — this is now settled, controlled background usage, not a default; no change in status.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Fifth chapter running clean. Ch. 15 kept Lloyd's self-management entirely physical and sensory under far more pressure than usual (mid-fight, badly hurt) and still didn't reach for filing/procedural language — a good sign this one may be fully retired rather than just resting.

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: Fifth chapter running without it. Not reached for in ch. 15 either; still safe to use if it arises naturally, not a default.

constructions.pattern: a statement capped with a trailing 'which was/is [flat judgment]' clause
constructions.example: which was true, and also the kindest thing she could have said to her just then; which was as much of a question as Edie generally asks
constructions.note: Three chapters clean now. A draft pass produced two bare trailing 'which was/wasn't [judgment]' closes in the Vail yard scene alone and both were split into separate short declaratives instead (the pattern that's replacing it, see long-sentence-run's contrast note). Treat any return to the bare trailing-'which' shape as a real lapse.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: Ch. 15 breaks the run as anticipated — it ends on a flat, undialogued catalogue of Lloyd's injuries (skull, ribs, arm) rather than an object-plus-dialogue close. Three chapters (12-14) still the longest run on this pattern; ch. 15 is deliberately not added to the chapters list.

closers.pattern: chapter ends on an image of something indifferent or inanimate personified as 'patient', waiting out time without hurry
closers.example: the night came down slow over the burnt manse... patient, working at the dark the way it works at everything, given enough time and no one to tell it to stop
closers.note: Spent at ch. 08-09 review; stayed spent through ch. 13. Do not return to 'patient' as a chapter-ending word.
